name: Pencil Drawing
visualIdentity: Fine graphite lines, exploratory contours and localized hatching on pale paper. Build volume with pencil marks, not broad gradients; keep pressure and texture coherent. Explicitly suited to intimate studies and sketch reveals.
suitableUses: Fits explanatory or illustrated narratives, product or editorial introductions, design process, architecture and natural history studies. Its intimate, hand-drawn look supports focused observation. These are stated use cases; fit for other subjects depends on the brief.
limitations: May be unsuitable when the subject needs color or a highly polished digital look. Keep hybrids graphite-only and uncluttered. Use chapter transitions only when story boundaries help; omit them when they obscure causality, disrupt a continuous shot or loop, or add spectacle without explanation.
palette: Suggested tokens for new artwork only: background #F5F2EA and foreground #383838, a monochrome pair with no gradient or accent hues. Preserve supplied, brand, reference and asset colors and their roles; use hatching, patterns or opacity for tone. Check contrast on actual composites; the stated 10.481 ratio applies only to opaque sRGB tokens.
motionAndInteraction: Reveal contours in drawing order, then hatching and optional lighter notes, or alternate a few designed variants. Avoid arbitrary noise. For video, use seekable composition time and readable holds; for interactive HTML, scroll may select story states or scrub chapter handoffs, with reverse progress restoring prior states. Support static or reduced-motion states.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, voiceover, effects, ambience or silence for the topic and explicit audio requirements; do not assume assets or mandatory layers. Keep speech clear, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and synchronize and inspect audio with picture.
assetRequirements: Prepare pale-paper textures, graphite brushes and layered contour and hatch artwork; use designed variants when needed. Exact subject assets, copy, fonts and audio are unspecified. Rough.js can supply seeded simplified contours or hachure, but not authentic pencil texture, pressure simulation, handwriting or authored drawing order; add material assets separately.
combinations: Works alone for intimate studies and sketch reveals. Style-024 graphite notes can add lighter labels and dimension marks in contour–hatching–notes order. Style-019 editorial framing can pair sketches with graphite typography and captions; keep paper texture within figures and pages flat. Avoid colored accents and clutter.
productionApproach: Canvas 2D owns drawing; Python and Pillow can prepare assets. Rough.js is optional for simplified seeded contours and hachure, not material simulation. GSAP or another suitable motion layer owns authored movement. HyperFrames is the primary composition/export pipeline; Remotion is only a documented fallback if unavailable or verified unable to meet a requirement. Keep visual and motion construction separate from export, use deterministic seekable time, and select tools for the style and fidelity.
